doc.title: Joe Wilder Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 12, 1998

title: Alec Wilder's sonata album and not listening to his own recordings
summary: Wilder tells of the Alec Wilder sonata album, not realizing Jim Marr wrote the liner notes, and says he is too critical to replay his recordings.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: I guess you’ve got a point there. I have some of them like this that are still in the cellophane. In fact, what recording was it, oh I did a classical album, Alec Wilder wrote a sonata for me. He had a knack of writing concerti and sonatas and things for his friends you know. And he really puts you to the test. So I recorded a thing, and I had forgotten who had written the liner notes mainly because I just glanced at them when the album came out. And it was Jim Marr had written the liner notes and we were over at Rutgers University and we were on the way home and he was talking about this album because they had played some excerpts of it, Ed Berger had played some of it. And he was saying yeah, you know such-and-such a thing about it. And he said, “when I wrote the liner © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -21-
notes — I was embarrassed. And when I got home I looked — I didn’t even realize it was Jim Marr who had written the liner notes. I didn’t tell him.
That you hadn’t even read them. Unbelievable.
But it was because I hadn’t played the album. Then I listened to it.
I think most musicians when they listen to their own work, they probably say —

We listen to it in the studio when we’re doing the final thing, sometimes before it’s even been mastered, and you listen to it, and usually, in my case I’ll hear something that I say well that wasn’t really right, and I wish I hadn’t done this that way or something like that. Not that this would have been any better or worse, but you listen and I’m very critical about that. I mean I hear things that I know could have been done better. And that disturbs me so I don’t bother to listen to it.
